name: OLAP (Online Analytical Processing)
definition: A way of storing and querying data in multidimensional form so that users can summarise and explore it quickly from many angles.
example: A manager views café sales by product, quarter and region, then drills from quarter to month.

name: OLTP (Online Transaction Processing)
definition: The everyday system that records each transaction as it happens, such as a sale or a booking.
example: A point-of-sale system that records each coffee sold.

name: Data Cube
definition: A multidimensional arrangement of data in which each cell holds a measure at the intersection of several dimensions.
example: A cube of sales with Product, Quarter and Region as its three dimensions.

name: Dimension
definition: A category by which data is viewed and grouped in analysis, often with a hierarchy of levels.
example: Time is a dimension with the levels year, quarter, month and day.

name: Measure
definition: The numeric value analysed in each cell of a data cube.
example: Sales in dollars or number of units sold.

name: Slice
definition: An OLAP operation that fixes one dimension at a single value, leaving a smaller table.
example: Slicing the sales cube at Region = Coast gives a Product by Quarter table.

name: Dice
definition: An OLAP operation that selects a sub-cube by choosing values on two or more dimensions.
example: Dicing for Coffee and Cake in Q3 and Q4 across both regions.

name: Drill-down
definition: Moving down a hierarchy to see more detailed data.
example: Going from quarterly sales to the three months in that quarter.

name: Roll-up
definition: Aggregating data up a hierarchy, or removing a dimension, to see a higher-level summary.
example: Summing months into quarters and quarters into a year.

name: Data Warehouse
definition: A large central store of consistent, historical data from many operational systems, organised for analysis and reporting.
example: A retailer loads nightly sales from 90 stores into one warehouse and compares years.

name: ETL (Extract, Transform, Load)
definition: The process of copying data from source systems, converting it to consistent formats and definitions, and loading it into a data warehouse.
example: Matching old and new product codes before loading sales history.

name: Data Integrity
definition: The accuracy, completeness, consistency and trustworthiness of data across its whole life.
example: Validation checks and access controls that stop a price of 5500 replacing 55.00.

name: Validation
definition: Checking that data is reasonable and allowed before it is accepted, for example by type, range, format or presence.
example: A range check rejects an age of 250.

name: Verification
definition: Checking that data has been entered or transferred correctly, such as by double entry or comparing totals with the source.
example: Two staff type the same figures and the system compares them.

name: Predictive Analytics
definition: Using patterns in historical data, with statistical methods or machine learning, to estimate what is likely to happen.
example: Forecasting Saturday's shuttle boardings from the temperature forecast.

name: Trend Line
definition: A line, usually the least-squares line of best fit, drawn through data to show its general direction and to make forecasts.
example: A spreadsheet chart trend line y = 14.4x + 296.5 fitted to twelve months of orders.

name: Outlier
definition: A value that lies far from the rest of the data; it may be an error or a genuine unusual event.
example: One $2,400 booking among bookings that are mostly under $110.

name: Aggregation
definition: Combining many records into a summary such as a total, average or count for each group.
example: Total takings for each month.

name: Truncated Axis
definition: A value axis that does not start at zero, which can exaggerate differences in a column chart.
example: A column axis from 90 to 95 makes 94% look four times as tall as 91%.

name: Cherry-picking
definition: Choosing only the data, date range or results that support a preferred conclusion.
example: Showing July to December sales growth and hiding the January to June decline.

name: Extrapolation
definition: Extending a pattern beyond the range of the data used to find it, which makes predictions less reliable.
example: Using a trend line built on 21 to 35°C data to predict boardings at 42°C.

name: Overplotting
definition: Marks on a chart overlapping so much that the pattern cannot be seen, common with very large datasets.
example: A scatter graph of a million points that looks like a solid blob.

name: Moving Average
definition: A series of averages of consecutive values, used to smooth short-term variation so that the trend shows.
example: A 3-month average of monthly orders.
